CONTROLLED BAY SERIES 1 of 3, the zero-bay reference. Tetracene, chrysene and triphenylene are all C18H12 with four rings and 0, 1 and 3 bays. Same formula, same ring count: only bay count and folding differ. Comparing across different formulas, which the phenanthrene job tried, confounds the bay with everything else at once.
CONTROLLED BAY SERIES 2 of 3. One bay, same formula and ring count as tetracene.

CONTROLLED BAY SERIES 3 of 3. Three bays, same formula. If the shift is roughly linear in bay count across these three, the bay is a real additive motif effect and the atlas needs it as a key. If it is not, the bay is not separable from shape and the atlas needs a different key altogether. Either answer settles the question.
Trio and duo coverage with no bays, so those classes appear in a second host molecule and their spread measures transfer rather than symmetry.

Benzene's e2g pair is doubly degenerate by symmetry: two modes that must land on the same wavenumber. In the committed C1 run they land on 619.1 and 642.2, split by 23 cm-1, more than twice the project tolerance. Either the geometry optimisation is too loose or something worse is true. This repeats benzene with gau_tight and nothing else changed; the split either collapses or it does not. Eight minutes to find out whether every number in this campaign carries a 20 cm-1 wobble.
